body.text: Getting your resume past Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) is crucial for Nigerian job seekers applying to modern companies. That's why I built a completely free ATS checker specifically designed for the Nigerian job market. This tool helps you understand how well your resume performs against the same systems used by major Nigerian employers like Dangote Group, GTBank, MTN Nigeria, and other top companies.
Why Nigerian Job Seekers Need an ATS Checker

Over 75% of large Nigerian companies now use ATS software to screen resumes before human recruiters see them. Companies like Access Bank, Nestle Nigeria, PwC Nigeria, and Unilever Nigeria rely on these systems to manage thousands of applications efficiently.

Without proper ATS optimization, your resume might never reach human eyes, regardless of your qualifications. This is particularly challenging for Nigerian job seekers who often format their CVs in ways that look good to humans but confuse ATS software.
Many Nigerian job seekers lose opportunities because their resumes contain formatting that ATS systems cannot read properly, such as tables, text boxes, or unusual fonts.

The checker extracts and analyzes how well ATS systems can read your resume text. It identifies formatting issues that might cause information to be lost or misinterpreted.
Keyword Optimization Score
The tool analyzes your resume against job descriptions common in the Nigerian market, checking for relevant industry keywords and skills that ATS systems prioritize.
Section Recognition
Our checker verifies that ATS systems can properly identify your contact information, work experience, education, and skills sections - crucial for Nigerian employers who rely on structured data.
Formatting Compatibility
The system flags formatting issues that commonly trip up ATS software, such as graphics, unusual fonts, or complex layouts that don't translate well to Nigerian corporate standards.
Common ATS Issues for Nigerian Resumes
Through testing hundreds of Nigerian resumes, I've identified the most frequent issues that prevent job seekers from passing ATS screening:
Poor Section Headers
Many Nigerian job seekers use creative section names like "My Journey" instead of standard headers like "Work Experience" that ATS systems recognize.
Complex Formatting
Resumes with tables, text boxes, or multiple columns often get scrambled when parsed by ATS software. This is especially common among Nigerian graduates who download fancy templates online.
Missing Keywords
Nigerian job seekers often undersell their skills by using local terminology instead of industry-standard keywords that ATS systems are programmed to find.
File Format Problems
Submitting resumes in formats like PNG images or password-protected PDFs prevents ATS systems from reading the content entirely.
Always save your resume as a simple PDF or Word document with standard fonts like Arial, Calibri, or Times New Roman for maximum ATS compatibility.

Step 4: Implement Recommendations

Step 5: Test Again
Re-upload your improved resume to see your new score and ensure all issues have been resolved.
Optimizing for Nigerian Company ATS Systems
Different Nigerian companies use various ATS platforms, but certain optimization strategies work across all systems:
Use Standard Section Headers
Stick to conventional headers like "Professional Experience," "Education," "Skills," and "Contact Information" that ATS systems are programmed to recognize.
Include Relevant Keywords

Study job postings from Nigerian companies in your field and incorporate their exact language into your resume. For example, if applying to banks like First Bank or UBA, include specific financial terminology they use.
Quantify Achievements
ATS systems are programmed to recognize numbers and metrics. Instead of "increased sales," write "increased sales by 25%" or "managed team of 8 staff members."
Match Job Requirements
Tailor your resume for each application by including keywords and skills mentioned in the specific job posting. This is crucial when applying to competitive Nigerian companies.
Industry-Specific ATS Tips for Nigeria
Banking and Finance

Nigerian banks like Zenith Bank, Ecobank, and Sterling Bank look for specific certifications and software knowledge. Include relevant acronyms like CFA, FRM, or software like SAP, Oracle, or Bloomberg.
Oil and Gas
Companies like Shell Nigeria, Chevron, and NNPC prioritize safety certifications and technical skills. Include certifications like NEBOSH, OSHA, or technical software knowledge.
Technology
Nigerian tech companies and fintech startups look for programming languages, frameworks, and tools. Be specific about your technical stack and include version numbers where relevant.
Telecommunications
MTN Nigeria, Airtel Nigeria, and Glo prioritize network management skills and telecommunications certifications. Include specific equipment knowledge and industry certifications.

Beyond the ATS Checker: Complete Resume Optimization

While our ATS checker identifies technical issues, remember that your resume still needs to impress human recruiters after passing the initial screening. Here's how to balance ATS optimization with human appeal:
Maintain Readability
Even with ATS optimization, your resume should be easy for Nigerian hiring managers to scan quickly. Use bullet points, consistent formatting, and clear section breaks.
Showcase Cultural Fit
Include volunteer work, community involvement, or leadership roles that resonate with Nigerian corporate culture and values.
Highlight Local Experience
When possible, emphasize experience with Nigerian companies, markets, or regulations that demonstrate your understanding of the local business environment.
Professional Summary Impact
Write a compelling professional summary that includes key ATS keywords while telling your career story in a way that appeals to Nigerian hiring managers.
Measuring Your ATS Optimization Success

body.text: Common Mistakes to Avoid
Based on analyzing thousands of Nigerian resumes, avoid these critical errors:
Over-optimization
Don't stuff your resume with so many keywords that it becomes unreadable. Maintain natural language flow while including relevant terms.
Ignoring Local Context
While optimizing for ATS, don't lose sight of Nigerian business culture and expectations. Include relevant local qualifications and experience.
One-Size-Fits-All Approach
Customize your resume for each application. The ATS systems at different Nigerian companies may prioritize different keywords and qualifications.
Neglecting Updates
Regularly test your resume with our ATS checker as you gain new skills or target different roles. Keep your optimization current with evolving ATS technology.
